clue.text: Sue newspapermen

definitions.meaning: to sue is to urge or push a claim
journalists collectively are known as the Fourth Estate's own name, the media of print

explanation.definitionFit: To urge a claim hard is to push it, and reporters as a body are named after the printing machine that runs off their papers.

clue.text: Maintain a lock-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Someone insists on keeping a lock-up garage or jail cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock-up' looks like one noun, a garage or cell, but it splits in two: a lock of hair, and 'up' as the signal that in a down entry the word reads from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to state it firmly, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: People responsible for actors clothing and furniture

definitions.meaning: theatre staff who help performers into their costumes
a kitchen sideboard with shelves for plates

explanation.definitionFit: Theatre wardrobe assistants who help actors change are called by this name, and so is a cupboard with open shelves for crockery.

clue.text: Looked round about tea-time, but wasn't offered anything to eat

indicators.note: round about says the word for looked surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to look hard is to stare; past tense stared
tea is traditionally taken at five o'clock, and five is V in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A guest gazes around the table at teatime but is given nothing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: British afternoon tea is traditionally at five o'clock, so 'tea-time' gives the Roman numeral V, which 'round about' puts inside STARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deprived of food has been left hungry, the passive sense of being kept from meals.

clue.text: He's a bad lot-or isn't as bad as he's made out

indicators.note: bad here tells us the letters of the words before it are spoiled, put into a wrong order

explanation.surface: A rogue protests that he isn't really as wicked as people make out.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'bad' is the anagram signal working on OR ISN'T AS; the first is part of the definition, a firebug being a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sets fires deliberately is a criminal, so certainly a villain.

clue.text: Drawing back a little way, and shy about it

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for shy goes round the other piece

parts.note: to shy is to throw, and so is to fling
an inch is a short distance

explanation.surface: Someone recoils a little, and is bashful about doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid, but here it is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Recoiling in fear or pain is pulling away, the present participle of a verb of shrinking.

clue.text: Check furs, treat splits

indicators.note: splits tells us the letters of the words before it are broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Inspect the furs and mend any tears in them.
explanation.definitionFit: To check a plan is to thwart or block it, the same as foiling it.

clue.text: Make a hole in some material

definitions.meaning: to bore through with a rotating tool

explanation.definitionFit: Boring with a rotating bit is the verb sense, and a strong twilled cotton fabric is the cloth sense.

clue.text: The head chef prepares this

definitions.meaning: the crown of the head, especially a bald one
a cook makes a savoury paste of liver or meat

explanation.definitionFit: An old word for the top of the skull, and, with an accent, a savoury meat paste a cook makes.

clue.text: He rates fools, getting endlessly irritated

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: sore means irritated or annoyed

explanation.surface: A man berates fools and grows annoyed with them without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He rates' looks like a man scolding, but rates means values: an official who sets values for tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuer who fixes a property's worth for tax or insurance purposes does exactly that job.

clue.text: Sum for which a doctor's been let in by relation

indicators.note: let in by says the doctor is admitted inside the relative

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: An aunt lets a doctor into the house, and there is a fee to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A total or quantity of money is a sum, a plain synonym.

clue.text: This may well cause the viewer great irritation

definitions.text: This may well cause the viewer great irritation

parts.words: This may well cause the viewer great irritation
parts.note: the viewer is not a television watcher but an eye, and the irritation is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid

explanation.surface: Something on screen annoys the person watching it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' suggests a television audience; read literally it is the one doing the seeing, the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A small inflamed swelling on the edge of an eyelid is genuinely sore for the eye.

clue.text: Sense there's agreement among rowing men

indicators.note: among says the agreement word sits inside the crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: Rowers come to a sensible agreement among themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Not a great work of art-though it could be

definitions.text: Not a great work of art-though it could be

parts.words: Not a great work of art-though it could be
parts.note: great is read as large: a tiny painting is not big, though it may be a masterpiece

explanation.surface: A modest painting may still prove to be a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' means excellent in the surface but large in the cryptic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A very small, finely detailed portrait painting is the art form meant.

clue.text: Seaside accommodation giving rise to complaint

indicators.note: accommodation means adjusting or adapting, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Holiday lodgings by the sea lead to a grievance from guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grumble about the lodgings, but it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment or illness.

clue.text: ACCESS taken here!

parts.note: the capitals suggest a credit card sign in a shop window, but it is simply where one gains admission

explanation.surface: A shop sign announcing that a credit card is accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: Access was a British credit card, often advertised in shop windows with 'Access taken here'; read plainly, access is entry, gained at a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway or way in is where admission into a building is obtained.

clue.text: Happy inside

explanation.definitionFit: Satisfied is one sense; stressed on the first syllable, the same letters mean the stuff held within.

clue.text: A doubter can be quite hard to influence

indicators.note: can be signals that the letters before it may be turned into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A sceptic may prove very hard to persuade.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stubborn and unyielding is difficult to sway.

clue.text: Orderly academicians with gun in hold up

indicators.note: in a down clue, hold up means the pieces are lifted and read upwards, backwards

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: Disciplined scholars armed with a gun stage a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' looks like a robbery; in this down entry it turns RA plus LUGER upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly and methodical behaviour is regular, steady and according to rule.

clue.text: Go back to help big family getting abuse

indicators.note: go back means the word for help is turned backwards

parts.note: aid is help
a tribe is a large family group or clan

explanation.surface: Returning to assist a large family earns only insults.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter verbal attack is a tirade of abuse.

clue.text: An island shows some coastal erosion always

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: An island always suffers some erosion along its coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Scottish island famous for its abbey founded by St Columba.

clue.text: Discourage rapid movement

definitions.meaning: to dishearten, as in hopes being destroyed
a sudden quick run or sprint

explanation.definitionFit: Hopes can be shattered and disheartened, and a sprint or rush is the noun sense.

clue.text: Thin as a result of using a down down

annotationWithheld.clue: Thin as a result of using a down down

clue.text: Dressed for spring

definitions.meaning: a wound is dressed when wrapped in a bandage

explanation.definitionFit: A bandaged wound has been tied up, and a leap is a jump forward.

clue.text: Air force

explanation.definitionFit: A tune can be a musical phrase, and stretching effort or tension is the other sense.

clue.text: Irrationality of French article concerning a child

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
re means concerning or about
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A treatise on the lack of logic in a French article about a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of reason or logic is absurdity, the absence of sound thinking.

clue.text: Expert? That's a joke!

definitions.meaning: first-rate, as in an ace shot

explanation.definitionFit: A first-class marksman is an ace, and a wisecrack is a quip.

clue.text: Supporters who are soft with the workers

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft
artisans are skilled manual workers

explanation.surface: Backers who are gentle along with the labour force.
explanation.definitionFit: Committed followers of a cause or guerrilla fighters back a side, a synonym of adherents.
